note: Sector estimates from the 2023–24 conflict assessment framework. Damage, losses and needs are distinct economic categories and are never summed. Sector estimates carry different cut-offs and methods within one assessment framework; the largest loss figures are macro-estimates rather than enterprise censuses. Null means not stated in the cited source, not zero.

sectors.label: Housing
sectors.detail: The single largest damage line; the private two-thirds of national needs is overwhelmingly housing and private economic assets.

sectors.label: Commerce, industry & tourism
sectors.detail: The single largest loss line. A lost season or a closed workshop has no owner, no repair chain and no project line - these losses were absorbed as household impoverishment and enterprise closure.

sectors.label: Environment & debris
sectors.detail: Core ecological envelope costed at US$299M and the rubble and debris envelope at US$145M within the needs figure; solid-waste sector damage put at US$11M.

sectors.label: Health
sectors.detail: The system lost the use of 40 hospitals and 42 primary-care centres.

sectors.label: Agriculture
sectors.detail: Assessed with FAO and CNRS-L covering crops (olives, citrus, banana), livestock, forestry, fisheries and aquaculture.

sectors.label: Transport
sectors.detail: Roughly 930 km of road affected; 21 of 29 Litani River bridges destroyed; 535 road sections assessed.

sectors.label: Electricity
sectors.detail: Network damage; restoration ran through EDL's emergency chains, not programme works, within the data window.

sectors.label: Municipal services
sectors.detail: On top of collapsed municipal finance - the tier's revenues had already fallen with the currency.

sectors.label: Education
sectors.detail: 594 public institutions were used as shelters, protecting families at the direct cost of more than 500,000 students' schooling - an institutional cost the monetary columns do not capture.
